# Slack renewal and cancellation guide (as of 2026-11-17)

Slack's current public customer terms and help pages set the defaults below. Your signed order form overrides them, and terms vary by contract date, region and negotiated order form. I could not retrieve Slack's own "cancel a plan" help article. The self-serve steps therefore come from third-party guides, and I've flagged them as such.

## 1. Default renewal behaviour
- **Auto-renews by default.** Unless an order form says otherwise, 
all subscriptions automatically renew, with no checkout or renewal order form needed, for periods of one year or the preceding term, whichever is shorter.

- **Renewal pricing.** The same terms say 
per-unit pricing in an automatic renewal term stays the same as in the prior term.
 This is the default only. A third-party source reports that Slack self-serve Business+ moved from $12.50 to $15 per user per month at the first renewal after 17 August 2025 (
Licenseware, checked 13 Nov 2026
). Check your own renewal quote.
- **Free subscriptions.** 
A free subscription continues until terminated, while a paid subscription has a term that may expire or be terminated.
 (This is from an archived version of the terms.)

## 2. Notice window
- **30 days.** Per Slack's customer terms, 
either party can give notice of non-renewal at least 30 days before the end of a subscription term.

- **Third-party corroboration.** Tropic describes 
30 days' opt-out notice as Slack's default
, and Licenseware lists 
30 days, written, under the Salesforce MSA
.
- **Conflicting source.** One reseller-style source claims Enterprise Grid agreements auto-renew with a 
90-day clause
. I couldn't verify this against Slack's own documents. It is plausibly a negotiated order-form term, so treat 30 days as the public default and confirm yours.
- **Cancel-by date.** Work it out as 
the renewal date minus the notice period.
 A 30-day default means your deadline is 30 days before term end.

## 3. How to cancel or give notice
**Self-serve plans (website purchase, card or self-serve invoice).** These steps are from third-party guides, not Slack's help center:
1. A workspace admin or owner needs web or desktop access. Sources disagree on whether admins can manage billing or only owners can (
one says only workspace owners
; 
another says owners or admins
). Confirm which role you need.
2. Open your workspace name, then Billing. Select 
Change subscription, then choose "Switch immediately to Free subscription" or "Switch to Free subscription upon renewal."

3. 
Preview the changes, tick the confirmation box and click Downgrade Slack.

4. Choosing the "upon renewal" option is the way to avoid paying for the next term while keeping paid features until then. Check the confirmation email.
